title: Secure network components, media, and endpoints: concept decisions 1
teachingQuestion: Which component, medium, admission condition, endpoint control, and shared dependency must work together for this network service to remain secure and available?
focalInsight: Network security combines infrastructure lifecycle, physical/media realities, admission control, endpoint persistence, and true independence of redundant paths.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Network Components
nodes.definition: Devices and services such as switches, routers, firewalls, access points, controllers, and supporting hardware that forward, enforce, or manage connectivity.
nodes.detail: Devices and services such as switches, routers, firewalls, access points, controllers, and supporting hardware that forward, enforce, or manage connectivity.
nodes.decision: Harden configuration/identity/management, inventory lifecycle, monitor health, and control changes for each component role.
nodes.failureExample: Default credentials on a network controller override sound downstream segmentation.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Every component has a forwarding/enforcement role and a management attack surface.

nodes.label: Transmission Media
nodes.definition: Physical paths—copper, fiber, radio, and related infrastructure—that carry signals with different tamper, interception, distance, attenuation, and interference properties.
nodes.detail: Physical paths—copper, fiber, radio, and related infrastructure—that carry signals with different tamper, interception, distance, attenuation, and interference properties.
nodes.decision: Choose/protect medium from location, threat, capacity, propagation quality, maintainability, and inspection needs.
nodes.failureExample: A cable run through public space is tapped despite strong application encryption metadata exposure.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Medium choice affects physical attack and availability properties.

nodes.label: Network Access Control
nodes.definition: Admission control using identity, device posture, location, role, certificate, and risk to allow, restrict, redirect, or quarantine network access.
nodes.detail: Admission control using identity, device posture, location, role, certificate, and risk to allow, restrict, redirect, or quarantine network access.
nodes.decision: Set policy and remediation/quarantine paths; reassess posture and log the admission decision.
nodes.failureExample: A device passes NAC then becomes compromised after admission.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: NAC decides admission; it does not guarantee ongoing endpoint safety.

nodes.label: Endpoint Security
nodes.definition: Host controls such as hardened configuration, EDR, host firewall, encryption, patching, integrity, logging, and response.
nodes.detail: Host controls such as hardened configuration, EDR, host firewall, encryption, patching, integrity, logging, and response.
nodes.decision: Apply and monitor controls after admission, with device lifecycle/identity ownership and incident containment.
nodes.failureExample: A compliant laptop loses patches and is exploited while still on its permitted VLAN.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Endpoint security remains active after network admission.

nodes.label: Redundancy
nodes.definition: Multiple components or paths intended to preserve service through a failure.
nodes.detail: Multiple components or paths intended to preserve service through a failure.
nodes.decision: Verify independence across power, conduit, provider, controller, firmware, identity, and failover behavior.
nodes.failureExample: Two links share one conduit or control plane and fail together during an outage.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Redundancy requires no critical common-mode dependency.

nodes.label: Support Lifecycle
nodes.definition: Vendor support, warranty, maintenance, inventory, replacement, patch, and retirement management for network assets.
nodes.detail: Vendor support, warranty, maintenance, inventory, replacement, patch, and retirement management for network assets.
nodes.decision: Track support status and replace/compensate for unsupported hardware/firmware before exposure becomes unfixable.
nodes.failureExample: An unsupported switch cannot receive a fix for a critical management-plane flaw.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Lifecycle status determines whether remediation is feasible.
